idea: Dinner decision-and-execution system for a busy parent: onboarding -> taste calibration -> ranked 3-dinner plan -> one-tap reasoned swaps -> consolidated traceable grocery list -> prep plan -> interruption-aware cooking mode -> one-tap feedback. Mobile-first web client over a deterministic TypeScript domain package and node:sqlite, zero runtime dependencies.
spec_digest: Dinner decision-and-execution system for an interrupted parent: onboarding -> 3-meal plan -> reasoned swap -> traceable grocery list -> interruption-aware cooking -> feedback.
Deterministic core is the product: quantities, units, aggregation, inventory subtraction, dietary filtering and ranking are pure tested code - never an LLM.
The differentiator nothing else ships: per-step active/unattended/continuous-attention time, safe stopping points, validated recovery, and cooking state that survives a kill.
Non-goals: no import, no grocery integration, no notifications, no nutrition, no social, no native build, no LLM in the authoritative path.
Taste: one hand, one dominant action per screen, <=3 choices, concrete countable copy, guilt-free language, honest uncertainty, zero engagement mechanics.

decisions.decision: Mobile-first web client instead of the brief's React Native + Expo.
decisions.why: Headless Linux build machine has no iOS simulator; an Expo client could not be run, interacted with or verified and would ship unproven. Domain package is client-agnostic so an RN port consumes it unchanged later.

decisions.decision: Catalog 55 -> 30 recipes; confirmed-only inventory (defer inference layer); greedy set-scoring instead of combinatorial plan search.
decisions.why: Independent taste judge scored scope-fits-night 3/10 and named the clock, not the idea, as the failure mode. Cuts protect the interruption-aware cooking loop and the traceable grocery list - the two things prior-art scouting confirmed nobody else ships. User endorsed all three.

decisions.decision: node:sqlite built-in, zero runtime dependencies; schema stays Postgres-shaped (UUIDs, UTC, integer cents, exact numeric quantities).
decisions.why: No PostgreSQL on this host and no sudo assumed. Verified node:sqlite works on Node 24.19 at kickoff. Postgres-shaped schema keeps the later migration mechanical.

decisions.decision: Build, not adopt or extend. Treat Mealie's aggregation design as the reference bar to clear.
decisions.why: Scout grep-verified that Mealie (AGPL-3.0, gate-fail for adoption) already ships deterministic conversion + fuzzy normalization + cross-recipe aggregation with traceability, and Grocy (MIT) ships conversion chains + pantry subtraction. That engine is table stakes, not the moat. Step-level interruption metadata, package-size selection and leftover optimization are unoccupied across all five products checked.

decisions.decision: ADOPT design-panel candidate B, 'Three Good Dinners' (AMBITIOUS brief), with six ideas grafted from the losers. Locked to .swarm/DESIGN.md, which is BINDING on every builder. Architecture: three strict layers (domain/ pure + server/ node:http+node:sqlite + web/ framework-free) run directly by Node 24 native type stripping, tsc --noEmit as the strict gate and never a build step. Six invariants are non-negotiable: (1) Rational bigint num/den is the only arithmetic type on authoritative paths, qty.ts the sole entry point; (2) timers stored as absolute UTC end instants, never remaining-seconds, so DoD 7 recovery is arithmetic; (3) every db.ts helper takes household_id as a required first argument and appends the WHERE itself, making an unscoped query inexpressible; (4) swap re-ranks against the frozen remaining two meals and never re-runs planset; (5) the catalog validation gate plus the ingredient-id/allergen-class cross-check land BEFORE the recipes, not in the proof wave; (6) recovery/panic guidance reads required per-step metadata only, never fabricated. Grafted steals: single copy module with numeric slots + one shared total-vs-active time renderer (makes DoD 6 a property of one helper); user grocery edits in a separate never-overwritten column; DESIGN.md as binding contract + tokens-only CSS rule; wave-0 node:sqlite smoke check on a real file DB; receipt/ledger grocery treatment; broadened e2e.loop asserting DoD 2 and DoD 6; ephemeral-port and db-path flags on the server entrypoint as test affordances against kill-test flake.
decisions.why: Blind judge scored B 45/50 vs C 42 and A 40 across must_haves/buildability/value/coherence/depth. B was the only candidate whose calibration module deliberately SELECTS attribute-spread cards (the spec demands deliberate variance, not just reactions), and the only one to catch that DoD 9 can fail via data rather than code - an allergen present but the dietary tag unverified - forcing the cross-check early. Its delighters are additive leaves on data the spec already forces it to persist, sequenced strictly after DoD is green and individually droppable, so they cannot compromise the core. C won coherence 10 for making aesthetics enforceable as code, which is exactly right for a headless build nobody can look at - hence four of the six steals come from C. Conductor gate re-derived all three judge totals from their axes, confirmed the declared winner is the argmax, probed the winning file plan for all 17 must-have surfaces, and checked the non-goal guards (zero runtime deps, no LLM on the authoritative path): 32/32 checks passed.

decisions.decision: The CONDUCTOR authors and commits the manifests (package.json, tsconfig.json, .gitignore) and runs the installs; builders never touch them. npm test = `tsc --noEmit` then `node --test 'tests/**/*.test.ts'`. Builder worktrees are provisioned at <target>/.wt/<item-id>, NOT under /tmp, and each builder runs `npm ci` there.
decisions.why: T-001's plan notes made it 'the manifest owner (sole exception)', but build-wave.js's builder brief hard-forbids touching manifests and instructs blocking instead - the item as planned was unbuildable, and the builder would have returned blocked. cycle.md step 4 already assigns manifests to the conductor, so the conductor writing them is in-contract, not a workaround. Separately: agent file-edit tools are confined to the session's allowed directories, so build-wave.js Step 0's /tmp worktree is git-writable but NOT edit-writable - every builder would stall part-way. Both mechanisms (in-repo worktree + npm ci, and the full tsc/node --test/node:sqlite pipeline) were proven BY THE CONDUCTOR on this host before any agent was dispatched; the wave then ran first-try clean.

decisions.decision: RecipeStep's nine required interruption fields use two names that differ from SPEC.md: `maximum_pause` (union {kind:'bounded',seconds} | {kind:'unlimited'}) instead of `maximum_pause_seconds`, and `timer_duration_seconds` (number | null) instead of `timer_duration`. `recovery_instruction` is likewise a union ({kind:'instruction',text} | {kind:'none_available'}) rather than a bare string. ACCEPTED as-is; the notes of T-008, T-009, T-010 and T-011 now carry the real names.
decisions.why: The must-have's substance is that all nine fields exist and are REQUIRED on every step - verified, all nine are non-optional readonly members. The identifiers are internal. Both renames are improvements: an explicit unit suffix, and explicit unions instead of null/sentinel magic, which is exactly what Invariant 6 ('no guidance available must be representable, not absent') asks for. Recorded rather than silently normalised because recipe JSON authored against the SPEC names would fail the catalog gate at 5am - the precise 'DoD 9 fails via data' failure the design panel predicted.

decisions.decision: Cycle 4 died between its merges and its verification gate: both builder branches were merged to master (860d034, ade40ef) but state.json, backlog.json, the journal and the runfile were never written, and no gate ran. Cycle 5 completed cycle 4 rather than starting new work — authored the gates from scratch, ran them, and closed the wave.
decisions.why: Merged-but-ungated code is the single most dangerous state this pipeline can be in: master carries work that LOOKS verified because it is committed, and hard rule 4 (green main) had never actually been checked. Dispatching a new wave on top would have compounded unverified work. The salvage rule in cycle.md step 2 covers dirty trees; this was the rarer case of a CLEAN tree whose bookkeeping was a cycle behind — detectable only because the commit messages said cycle 4 while state.json said cycle 3.

decisions.decision: T-002's domain/src/ingredients.ts is CUT from scope. catalog.ts (landed by T-008) already owns the curated ingredient registry — aliases, allergen classes, densities, per-item weights — sourced from data/ingredients.json. normalize.ts consumes IngredientRegistry as a parameter instead of owning a second table.
decisions.why: A second curated table would be a second source of truth, which is precisely the data-drift failure Invariant 5 exists to prevent. Ruled at cycle 6 dispatch time and recorded in the in-flight marker; formalised here because the cycle that made the ruling died before it could write a journal block.

decisions.decision: Cycle 6 was killed mid-wave by the pacer's 600s background-task ceiling ("Background tasks still running after 600s; terminating", runs/pacer.log 22:55Z). This session RESUMED cycle 6 rather than opening cycle 7: merged wave-006-T-002 (complete and committed by its builder), salvage-committed the T-006 builder's uncommitted worktree files, merged those too, then authored and ran both verification gates.
decisions.why: The in-flight marker cycle 6 wrote at dispatch (D-8's lesson from cycle 4) worked exactly as designed — it named the branches, the worktrees and the recovery procedure, so this session lost no time diagnosing. The T-006 builder had written filters.ts, score.ts and filters.test.ts but not score.test.ts; that work was coherent and self-contained (imports only frozen modules), so salvaging beat discarding 1,370 lines and rebuilding. What the salvage CANNOT do is invent the missing regression tests — filed as T-029 rather than papered over.

decisions.decision: Cycle 7 dispatched its two builders as DIRECT, FOREGROUND Agent calls editing the main working tree under strictly disjoint file scopes — no build-wave workflow, no worktrees, no builder branches. Both builders were forbidden to run any git command; the conductor committed.
decisions.why: KI-4 killed cycles 4 and 6 mid-wave. This cycle established the mechanism: bin/swarm-pacer.sh spawns `claude -p` synchronously with NO timeout of its own (verified by reading lines 232-260), so the 600s guillotine is purely the harness background-task wait ceiling (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS, default 600000) applied at turn end. Foreground agents are part of the turn, not background tasks, so the ceiling never applies. The wave ran 424s and 356s — both would have been at risk, and the T-029 builder in particular was still working at the 356s mark. This is a prompt-side workaround costing nothing; the durable fix is still in the pacer and still belongs in the morning report.

decisions.decision: A backlog item whose deliverable is a TEST FILE is gated by MUTATION TESTING, not by a green suite. T-029 was verified by injecting 13 deliberate defects into score.ts one at a time and requiring the committed suite to go red for each.
decisions.why: A file of assert.ok(true) passes npm test. For T-029 specifically the whole point was that score.ts had zero committed coverage, so accepting `suite green` as evidence would have re-created the exact hole the item existed to close. The method paid for itself immediately: 11 of 13 mutants died, but two survived and revealed a precise, non-obvious gap (penalties are read back from the engine rather than pinned as literals, so penalty-amount drift mutates test and engine in lockstep). That gap is invisible to every other form of review.

decisions.decision: T-005 was flagged route_class 'core' at cycle-9 pick time, which routes it to fable and exempts it from the gear-2 demotion under the fable guard. T-034, its successor, inherits the flag.
decisions.why: The flag was absent at plan time, inconsistently with every sibling module: T-002, T-003, T-004 and T-006 all carry it. preferences.ts is an authoritative-path module - it persists Rational signals and its output decides, through filters.ts, what a household can ever be shown - so it meets the same correctness-core standard those siblings meet. Recorded rather than applied silently because the flag also has a pacing consequence (it buys fable in a gear that would otherwise demote to sonnet), and a routing choice that spends more budget should be auditable. Test applied before flagging: would I flag it in gear 5 too? Yes.

decisions.decision: The cycle-9 T-005 gate deliberately probed BEYOND the defect the item failed on: as well as re-running the cycle-8 probe verbatim, it built a second, realistic 12-recipe catalog with broad flavour tags. The item passed the first probe and failed the second.
decisions.why: The cycle-8 fix direction named three axes as 'distinctive' - protein, cuisine, flavour - and the first two are, but the FlavourTag vocabulary contains 'savoury', 'mild' and 'fresh'. A gate that only re-ran the original probe would have marked this item done and shipped the identical product-breaking failure on a different axis, invisibly, because the original probe's catalog carried no flavour tags at all. The lesson generalises past this item: when a fix works by RECLASSIFYING inputs, the gate must test the reclassification against realistic data, not just re-run the case that failed - otherwise the gate only proves the specific counterexample was handled. This is also the second time in two cycles that composing modules (preferences x filters) found what neither module's own suite could, reinforcing the cycle-8 finding.

decisions.decision: Cycle 10 was killed by a SESSION USAGE LIMIT, not by KI-4's 600s background-task ceiling. This session resumed cycle 10 rather than opening cycle 11: salvage-committed T-034's two modified files, authored a fresh 23-check gate against them, and closed the wave. T-007, whose builder produced ZERO files, is returned to todo with attempts LEFT AT 0 rather than incremented.
decisions.why: runs/cycle-1787102668.json records is_error=true, result "You've hit your session limit · resets 3:20am (UTC)", num_turns 38, duration 831s — the cycle was cut off mid-wave by the account's 5h session cap, and the three pacer spawns that followed (01:43, 01:48, 01:54Z) each died in under 500ms with the identical message and $0 cost. That is a DIFFERENT failure mode from KI-4 and it is filed separately as KI-6; attributing it to KI-4 would have sent the next cycle chasing a timeout that was not the cause. attempts is deliberately NOT incremented on T-007 because cycle.md's attempts+1 rule exists to escalate items whose BUILD failed; T-007's build never ran. Incrementing it twice for conductor-session deaths would blocked-cap a critical-path item for a reason that has nothing to do with its code.

decisions.decision: The cycle-11 T-007 gate failed 4 of 52 checks on its first run. All four were defects in the GATE, not in the code, and each was proven so with a recorded diagnostic BEFORE any check was touched. Rev1 and its failing output are kept on disk beside the corrected rev2 (58/58).
decisions.why: Loosening a check that just went red is exactly how a run starts overclaiming, so the bar for editing one is evidence, not plausibility. (1) A1 searched swap.ts for the string "planset" and tripped on the module's own doc comment "This module does not import planset.ts AT ALL" — three occurrences, all comments, none an import; corrected to search comment-stripped source. (2) E2 demanded every swap reason yield alternatives; a hand-derived count independent of swap.ts showed ZERO strictly-cheaper candidates exist because all three planned meals are already the cheapest band, so returning nothing is correct — corrected to excuse only provably-empty reasons and to exercise cheaper against a high-band outgoing meal instead. (3) E5c required the pantry's target dish to rank first; five variants share its exact required-ingredient set, so all tie at 100% owned and the order among them is settled correctly by other terms. (4) E8 — the one that mattered — cloned the outgoing meal to prove overlap is scored against the frozen pair, but the outgoing meal shared ALL EIGHT of its required ingredients with that pair, so overlap 1 was the right answer to the wrong question; rebuilt on a hand-assembled plan using only the outgoing meal's EXCLUSIVE ingredients, which now scores 0 exactly like a disjoint candidate while a frozen-meal echo scores 1. The rebuilt E8 is a stronger test than the original, and only exists because the first one failed. A gate that never fails is not being pointed at anything.

decisions.decision: DoD 6's total+active pairing requirement applies to user-facing duration displays, not to a field that is definitionally active-only. prep.active_time_blocks[] is exempt; a total_seconds without an active_seconds remains a hard failure anywhere it appears.
decisions.why: rev1 of the cycle-12 gate asserted the pair on EVERY object carrying active_seconds and failed on prep.active_time_blocks. domain/src/prep.ts defines ActiveTimeBlock as "a maximal run of index-contiguous steps each with active_duration_seconds > 0" — a breakdown of where hands-on work sits, with no total to state and nothing conflated, which is the confusion DoD 6 exists to prevent. The check was wrong, not the code. rev1 and its failing output are kept on disk (cycle-012-gate-rev1.mjs, cycle-012-verify-wave-rev1-FAILING.txt); rev2 narrows the rule and adds F2c asserting the exemption can never widen beyond that one shape. The missing time_label is NOT waived — it is filed as T-040 and asserted by F3b.

decisions.decision: MealView carries plan_meal_id, beyond the frozen cycle-12 contract. Accepted.
decisions.why: The T-014 builder raised it rather than working around it: POST /api/feedback and POST /api/cooking/sessions both require plan_meal_id, and db.ts enforces it with a real foreign key — but no frozen view exposed one, so no client could ever supply a valid value and both routes were unreachable. Adding the field is the minimal correct fix. The contract text is amended for the screens still to be built.

decisions.decision: T-042 is fixed by moving the onboarding defaults to 60 min total / 30 min active - the smallest pair of ALREADY-OFFERED option values under which the shipped catalog yields three dinners. The two other options its acceptance left open were ruled out by the conductor BEFORE dispatch, and the builder was told so: the time ceiling must not become soft/advisory, and the default must not become "No limit".
decisions.why: The item as filed offered three routes (change the defaults, stop the ceiling being an absolute hard filter, or add fast recipes) and letting a builder choose would have risked the one that breaks an invariant. The ceilings are absolute hard filters by locked domain invariant (T-006); softening one to make a default work would have traded a visible empty plan for an invisible broken promise, which is strictly worse for a parent who set a time limit because they have no time. Defaulting to "No limit" erases the question the screen exists to ask. Adding genuinely fast recipes is the real cure and is T-010/T-011 - once the catalog has them, the default can drop back toward 30/15. Gate check W5 pins the ruling: the old 900s/1800s ceilings must STILL exclude all six recipes, so a future attempt to fix an empty plan by weakening the filter fails the gate.

decisions.decision: The cycle-13 gate derives the onboarding defaults by PARSING web/js/onboarding.js and resolving the identifier to its const binding, then builds its live households from those parsed values. It never hardcodes 3600/1800.
decisions.why: A gate that asserts "a 3600s/1800s household gets three meals" proves the server works; it does not prove the SHIPPED DEFAULT works, which is the entire content of T-042. Had the builder edited only the option list and left the state initialiser at 30/15 - a plausible near-miss, since the defaults were duplicated magic strings and that duplication is exactly how the defect arose - a hardcoded gate would have passed while the product stayed broken. Parsing the file makes the check point at the defect rather than at the expected answer. It also verified the builder's single-source-of-truth refactor for free: W1a/W1b report the value came via DEFAULT_TOTAL_TIME/DEFAULT_ACTIVE_TIME.

decisions.decision: Gate rev1 failed 8 of 33. Seven were defects in the GATE, one was arithmetic I got wrong; all were proven so by a recorded read-only diagnostic (cycle-013-diag.mjs -> .swarm/runs/cycle-013-diagnostic.txt) BEFORE any check was edited. rev1 and its failing output are kept on disk beside rev2.
decisions.why: Five checks read body.shortfall when the API nests the plan at body.plan.shortfall - the response carried a completely correct, fully-derived explanation and my accessor could not see it. One check (A3b) asserted a 1200s active ceiling produces a partial plan; the catalog actually has THREE recipes at or under 1200s active (960/1080/1140), so a full plan was the right answer and my count was wrong - replaced with 1080s, which clears exactly two. One (A9) used a regex that spanned newlines and matched whole blocks of TypeScript source rather than string literals. One (A9b) searched for the literal "hands-on limit" in reasons.ts, but that phrase is COMPOSED at runtime from a code-dependent dimension word, so a correct implementation failed a literal search - replaced with the stronger exclusivity claim that the distinctive phrase appears in exactly one module. The rule this run keeps re-earning: the bar for editing a red check is a recorded diagnostic, never plausibility - and a gate whose checks never fail is not pointed at anything.

decisions.decision: Built a DOM shim (.swarm/runs/domshim.mjs) so web screens are EXECUTED under node against the live server and asserted on rendered text, replacing the source-grep gates used for every previous web item.
decisions.why: A text gate cannot distinguish "the file contains the word shortfall" from "the user sees the shortfall sentence" - which is exactly the KI-7 residual cycle 13 left open. The shim was validated against the already-shipped onboarding.js BEFORE being used to judge new code (459 chars of real copy, 15 tappables), so a shim gap could not be mistaken for a product defect. It caught a severe defect no grep would have found: the grocery ledger printing raw rationals.

decisions.decision: I wrote gate rev1 into the target working tree while the build wave was live. The T-016 builder found and ran it during development. All rev1 PASS results for T-016 are treated as contaminated and were discarded; rev2 was authored after code freeze and is the evidence of record.
decisions.why: Hard rule 2 says builders never see the verify check, because an agent that knows the check can code to the check. Writing the gate into the shared tree mid-wave defeated that. The builder disclosed it unprompted, which is how it was caught. Fix for future cycles: author gates only after the wave returns, or hold them outside the target tree until then. rev1 and its output are preserved on disk as cycle-014-gate-rev1-CONTAMINATED.mjs.

decisions.decision: Cycle 15 died after dispatching its two foreground builders but before any bookkeeping: the working tree held cook.js (557 lines), cook.css and edits to plan.js/grocery.js/router.js/index.html, none of it committed, and no gate had run. This session RESUMED cycle 15 rather than opening cycle 16 — judged the tree coherent, salvage-committed it as 5622810, then authored and ran the verification gate from scratch.
decisions.why: The in-flight marker written at dispatch (D-8's lesson) again paid for itself: it named both items, their exact file scopes and the salvage procedure, so no time went to diagnosis. Coherence was judged on evidence, not optimism — the full suite was green on the dirty tree, every new import resolved to a function that already existed (api.js createCookingSession/getCookingSession/postCookingEvent, and the three server routes), and no file was half-written. Opening a fresh cycle would have left two finished screens sitting unverified on disk, which is the merged-but-ungated state D-8 exists to prevent.

decisions.decision: Cycle 15's gate went through two revisions, and every rev1 failure was a fault in the gate, not the product. rev1 is preserved unmodified beside rev2 with its output. The three faults: it searched for the rendered amount under a lowercase display_name and inside the wrong node; it opened the bottom sheet of a to-taste line, which correctly has neither an amount nor an editor; and its attention-warning probe drove the session through every step, completing it, so the four checks that followed ran against a finished session and failed for that reason alone. A separate diagnostic (cycle-015-diagnostic.txt) proved each before rev2 was written.
decisions.why: A gate that fails for its own reasons is worse than no gate: it either gets believed, and real work is re-queued for nothing, or it gets waved through, and the next false pass is invisible. Writing the diagnostic first — dump the actual DOM, list which recipes actually have continuous-attention steps, replay the rejected timer payload against a fresh session — turned five ambiguous FAILs into five understood harness bugs in one run. The rule this run keeps re-learning: when a gate fails, find out WHY it failed before touching either side.

decisions.decision: The T-043 gate imports no domain code at all — it reads data/recipes/*.json off disk, re-derives every expected quantity with BigInt rational arithmetic written inside the gate, and compares against the live HTTP response.
decisions.why: The builder's own tests import scale.ts, the module whose correctness is the question. A bug inside scale.ts would pass their tests and mine both if mine reused it. Re-deriving independently also caught that the checks were worth having: G4 exists purely to prove the comparison is not a factor-1 tautology, and G5/G6 (identity at size 4, exact thirds at size 3) cover the two ways a scaling fix usually goes wrong — double-scaling and integer truncation.

decisions.decision: The active-time-block label is PRODUCED in domain/src/reasons.ts and ATTACHED at the route encode boundary in server/src/routes.ts — it is not stored on the domain ActiveTimeBlock type.
decisions.why: DoD 6's mechanism is one shared time renderer, and reasons.ts already owns the only duration-to-text function in the product; a second minute formatter anywhere is precisely the drift the rule exists to prevent. But ActiveTimeBlock is derived recipe data carrying no presentation text, and pushing a label into it would churn unrelated deepEqual assertions in prep.test.ts for no correctness gain. Produce in the domain, attach at the wire. Ruled BEFORE dispatch and recorded in .swarm/runs/cycle-018-inflight.md so the builder could not have reverse-engineered it from the gate. [id corrected cycle 20: this entry was filed as a second D-18, colliding with cycle 12's MealView ruling. Renumbered to D-28 — the cycle-12 entry keeps D-18 because prior journal blocks cite it under that id.]

decisions.decision: Swap arity is generalised from exactly-3 to 1-3 meals. SwapRequest.meals is readonly SwapMealInput[], SwapResult.unchanged and the two frozen parameters are readonly SwapMealInput[], and the frozen context MAY BE EMPTY. DESIGN.md Invariant 4's wording ('re-ranks against the frozen remaining TWO meals') is now imprecise for 1- and 2-meal plans; its SUBSTANCE - swap ranks only against the frozen remaining meals and never re-runs planset - is unchanged and was gate-verified (S3: swap.ts still does not import planset). Recorded as a decision rather than edited into DESIGN.md, which is binding and conductor-owned.
decisions.why: KI-9 (high, open since cycle 12) was not a route bug: server/src/routes.ts required rows.length === 3 because domain/src/swap.ts typed meals as a fixed 3-tuple. A time-limited household is exactly the household the planner gives a partial plan to, so the users most likely to get a short plan were the users who could then never change it - a permanent dead end. The ruling was made BEFORE dispatch and written to .swarm/runs/cycle-019-inflight.md so the builder could not reverse-engineer it from the gate: no tuple padding, no casts, no planset re-run, no weakening of the 409, slot validation stays real. The empty-frozen-set semantics were checked in the code first and PINNED as correct (overlap 0, protein/cuisine diversity 1, no fabricated shares_ingredients fact) so a builder could not 'fix' behaviour that was already right.

decisions.decision: The ~30-live-item cap is left BREACHED at 34, not met by dropping work. One item was dropped on merit (T-025). The remaining 34 all cover a SPEC must-have, a definition-of-done clause, or a filed defect.
decisions.why: The cap exists to stop a backlog from accumulating noise. This backlog is not noisy — it is larger than the clock. Dropping four real items to reach 30 would shrink the ledger, not the work, and would hide a genuine shortfall from the morning report. The honest artifact is an over-cap backlog with the shortfall named: T-010/T-011 (24 of the 30 spec'd recipes) and T-017 (the grocery ledger screen, which alone gates T-021, T-024 and T-062) are L/M-effort and the weekly governor has clamped the reachable gear ceiling to 2 for the rest of this run.

decisions.decision: The T-053 gate asserts client output against the DOMAIN's own combined_label, computed live by importing domain/src/reasons.ts — never against a literal string typed into the gate.
decisions.why: A gate that hardcodes "26 min total, 16 min hands-on" tests the gate author's memory of the spec. A gate that asks the domain tests the product's internal agreement, which is what DoD 6 actually asserts. It paid immediately: the sweep of 1743 (total,active) pairs caught a second live defect nobody had filed — the visible spans never implemented the "under 1 min" branch that the domain and the aria-label both had, so sub-minute durations rendered "0 min total" to the eye and "under 1 min total" to a screen reader. A hardcoded 26/16 gate would have gone green over it.

decisions.decision: The T-053 gate includes H10, a LAYOUT check: the separator must not be a bare text node directly under .time-info while that element is still display:flex with a gap.
decisions.why: .time-info is a flex row, so the two spans already sat apart on screen — the defect a user actually saw was a MISSING COMMA, not missing space. The obvious fix (append ", " as a child of the container) would have made textContent correct while rendering a floating comma as its own flex item with gap on both sides: "26 min total , 16 min hands-on". H10 is the check that stops a fix that passes the acceptance and looks wrong on the phone. The builder independently avoided the trap by putting the separator inside the total span; H10 now pins it.

decisions.decision: A RECYCLE cycle does not increment counters.consecutive_no_value. It stays at 1 (earned by cycle 21's failed T-038 gate) rather than rising to 2 at cycle 22.
decisions.why: The churn breaker exists to detect a TARGET thrashing - repeated attempts at value that produce none. A recycle cycle is conductor context hygiene mandated by hard rule 7 at cycles_since_recycle>=25; it dispatches no agent and attempts no item, so counting it as a failed attempt would corrupt the signal with the conductor's own bookkeeping. Concretely it would have tripped the >=2 forced work-type switch at cycle 23, banning a build wave for a reason that has nothing to do with the target. Recorded rather than applied silently because it is a deliberate deviation from the mechanical reading of cycle.md's churn-breaker sentence ('a cycle with no verified-value outcome increments it'), and a conductor loosening its own thrash detector should be auditable.

decisions.decision: T-017 is CLOSED as done on a fresh 18-check conductor gate, of which 3 checks are recorded NOT RUN (unreachable by design) rather than passed or failed. The item is done at 15/15 of what is reachable, and REPORT.md must carry the 3 unreachable clauses as unverified surface.
decisions.why: T-017 sat todo with attempts:1 for nine cycles on the strength of ONE cycle-14 failure (R21, raw rationals) that T-052 had already fixed at cycle 15 — nobody re-ran the item. Re-running it cost one cycle-slot of conductor time and closed a p1/H must-have that was gating T-021, T-024 and T-062. The three not-run checks are the honest part: two need catalog package data that does not exist (T-065) and one needs an inferred-inventory write path that D-2 deliberately cut (T-066). Rendering them as PASS would have been a fake gate; rendering them as FAIL would have blamed the screen for a data and scope gap it cannot fix. cycle.md step 6.5 says a check you could not run is reported as not-run, and this is what that looks like in practice.

decisions.decision: Package-size selection, estimate labelling and leftover/surplus optimisation are IMPLEMENTED IN THE ENGINE AND UNREACHABLE IN THE PRODUCT, because data/ingredients.json ships zero package options for all 97 ingredients. Filed as T-065 at priority 1.
decisions.why: D-4 named package-size selection and leftover optimization as two of the three differentiators the prior-art scout found unoccupied across all five competitor products checked. packaging.ts implements both and is unit-tested; routes.ts encodes package_label, is_estimate and expected_surplus onto every grocery line. But the catalog has no package data, so a live 22-line grocery list measured this cycle had 0 estimated lines, 0 lines with surplus and null package labels throughout. The moat is written and switched off. This was invisible to every prior cycle because the unit tests supply their own package fixtures — only a gate driving the REAL catalog through the REAL server could see it, which is exactly why the conductor authors gates against live data rather than fixtures.

decisions.decision: A build item whose acceptance names a USER-VISIBLE observable must have its file scope derived from that observable at pick time, not copied from the stored files_hint.
decisions.why: T-065 was dispatched this cycle with files_hint [data/ingredients.json, tests/packaging.test.ts], taken verbatim from the backlog and from the item's own claim that "the engine is done". Its acceptance, though, ends "...A grocery list for a real plan then contains at least one line with a non-null package_label" — an observable that lives behind domain/src/catalog.ts and server/src/routes.ts, neither of which was in scope, and routes.ts was in the concurrent builder's scope besides. The data authoring was excellent and verified 6/6; the item still failed its gate 3/3 on the half that matters to a user. Cost: one item's worth of wave capacity at gear 2, where the cap is 2. The stored files_hint is a planning-time guess; the acceptance is the contract.

decisions.decision: npm test now typechecks the client: `typecheck` = `typecheck:node && typecheck:web`, with tsconfig.web.json (allowJs+checkJs+strict, lib dom) covering web/js/**.
decisions.why: Every 'typecheck passes' claim made about a client file before cycle 25 was true but vacuous — tsc had never read those files. Wiring the second project into the existing test_cmd rather than leaving it a side script is what makes the guarantee load-bearing: hard rule 4's green-main check now covers the client. The conductor made the package.json edit itself, since manifest files are excluded from builder scope.

known_issues.desc: Kickoff step-5 settings.json edit DENIED by the harness (recurrence of the SWARM-side KI-2 seen on the moon run for 24 consecutive runs). Two consequences: (a) permissions.additionalDirectories stays [], so every headless cycle depends on swarm-pacer.sh passing --add-dir /opt/targets/dinner explicitly - a relaunch that omits it will stall on permission prompts; (b) bin/swarm-budget.sh and bin/swarm-playbook.sh remain unallowlisted, so the budget probe and playbook parser cannot run from a headless conductor and must be worked around (budget seeded from the last real probe; playbook apply_mode read by direct file read). SWARM-side tooling gap, not a target defect. Hard rule 5 forbids fixing it from inside a run - it belongs in the morning report.

RE-OPENED at cycle 5 (was mislabelled RESOLVED-BY-DRIFT at cycle 3). The weekly governor zero-envelope blind spot in bin/swarm-weekly-from-allocator.sh: heat is computed as 100*swarm_used/(swarm_used+allow_overall), so a zero denominator DISENGAGES the governor. At cycle 3 swarm_used_pct had drifted 0 -> 4 and I recorded the bug as resolved. At cycle 5 it fell back to 0 with allow_overall_pct 0 and posture "trickle", so the feeder would disengage the governor again — precisely when restraint matters most. The ceiling held at 2 this cycle ONLY because a second, independent signal was hot (raw account 52.0% weekly at 24.65% week-elapsed => heat 2.11). Drift is not a fix. Correct behaviour: u+a <= 0 must mean MAXIMUM heat, not "unconfigured". Hard rule 5 forbids the fix mid-run; morning report.

SWARM-side, workflows/build-wave.js. Its builder Step 0 hardcodes a /tmp worktree (mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/wave-<id>.XXXXXX"). On this host, agent file-edit tools are confined to the session's allowed directories (/opt/swarm, /opt/targets/<target>), so a /tmp worktree is writable by git but NOT by the builder's own Write/Edit tools: every builder would provision successfully, then stall or fail part-way through its first edit. Worked around this cycle by a conductor `context` override pointing the worktree at <target>/.wt/<item-id> (gitignored) plus an `npm ci` there; the wave then ran clean first try. The durable fix is to derive the worktree root from projectDir in build-wave.js rather than TMPDIR. Second, smaller gap in the same file: it passes the backlog's effort value straight to agent({effort}), but the backlog uses S/M/L while the harness expects low/medium/high - the conductor mapped L->high at dispatch. Hard rule 5 forbids editing the script mid-run; both belong in the morning report.

SWARM-side. The headless pacer kills a cycle's background tasks after 600s ("Background tasks still running after 600s; terminating" — runs/pacer.log 2026-08-18T22:55Z), but build-wave's own duration budget is 2700s. Any wave whose builders run past 10 minutes is guillotined mid-flight: cycle 6 lost its workflow return, its journal block and one builder's test file this way, and cycle 4 died the same way earlier in the run. The conductor's in-flight marker makes this RECOVERABLE (cycle 6 was resumed and closed cleanly), but every occurrence costs a cycle and can leave merged-but-ungated code. Fix direction: set CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS to match the wave budget in bin/swarm-pacer.sh, or have the pacer read the wave-duration table. Hard rule 5 forbids the fix mid-run; morning report.

RESOLVED at cycle 10 (T-034), both halves. History: applyCalibrationReaction(never_recommend) wrote an absolute-exclusion lock (value -1, confidence 1) to EVERY attribute axis, so one tap hard-excluded most of a catalog sharing none of the card's character. Cycle 9 fixed the generic axes (spice, richness, method, effort, texture) but LEFT flavour locked, and FlavourTag carries catalog-wide members, so one tap on a savoury card still left only 3/12 survivors. Cycle 10 dropped flavour from never_recommend_lock_attributes (a one-line config change; the lock is now exactly protein+cuisine). CONDUCTOR-VERIFIED by a fresh 23-check gate (SWARM/runs/cycle-010-gate-T034.mjs, output .swarm/runs/cycle-010-verify-T-034.txt, 23/23): taps on all three generic members (savoury 8/12 holders, mild 2/12, fresh 3/12) now exclude ZERO dishes; protein and cuisine kin plus the reacted dish are still absolutely excluded (10/12 survive, exactly the 2 kin fall); flavour signals are still emitted, still negative (-9/10), still durable, and sit below the 1/2 hard-filter gate; and a corroborated flavour signal (-9/10, confidence 4/5) STILL hard-excludes all 8 savoury dishes, proving the axis was not defanged. Residual trade-off recorded, not hidden: distinctive flavour tags (garlicky, smoky, umami, ...) now also fall through the generic path, so a tap on a smoky dish no longer vetoes other smoky dishes. The durable fix is a curated distinctive/generic partition of FlavourTag, filed as T-036 and NOT built tonight.

SWARM-side / account-side, DISTINCT FROM KI-4. The account's 5-hour SESSION limit terminated cycle 10 mid-wave and then killed three consecutive pacer spawns outright. Evidence: runs/cycle-1787102668.json (is_error true, "You've hit your session limit · resets 3:20am (UTC)", num_turns 38, duration_ms 831019, cost $8.49) followed by runs/cycle-1787103828.json, cycle-1787104138.json and cycle-1787104455.json — each num_turns 1, duration under 500ms, cost $0.00, same message. Consequences: (a) a cycle can die from the session cap at ANY point regardless of wave duration, so the in-flight marker (D-8) is the only thing standing between this and merged-but-ungated code; (b) the pacer has no session-limit awareness — it kept respawning every ~5 min into a hard wall, converting a usage pause into a stream of failed cycles in pacer.log; (c) neither the window probe (rho 0.50, cool) nor the weekly governor (heat 2.58, hot) models the SESSION cap, so the pacing machinery could not have predicted or prevented this. Fix direction: teach bin/swarm-pacer.sh to parse the session-limit message out of the cycle result JSON and back off until the quoted reset time instead of respawning on its fixed interval. SWARM-side, hard rule 5 — recorded, not edited mid-run; belongs in the morning report.

The DEFAULT first-run path produces zero dinners. web/js/onboarding.js:174-175 pre-selects total 30 min / active 15 min, and every authored recipe is 26-78 min total and 16-27 min active, so the hard time filter excludes the whole catalog: POST /api/plans returns 201 with meals: [] and no explanation, and GET /api/plans/current then answers "This household has no plan yet." — which is false. Found by the cycle-12 live-look pass and INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED by the conductor (.swarm/runs/cycle-012-verify-lookfindings.txt lines 4-14; control household with no ceilings returns 3 meals). Filed as T-041 (make the failure honest) + T-042 (stop it happening on the default path). This is the single most important thing to fix next: the product currently greets a default user with nothing. RESOLVED at cycle 13 by T-042 + T-041, CONDUCTOR-VERIFIED by a fresh 40-check gate (/opt/swarm/runs/cycle-013-gate.mjs, output .swarm/runs/cycle-013-verify-wave.txt, 40/40). The onboarding defaults now derive from single DEFAULT_TOTAL_TIME/DEFAULT_ACTIVE_TIME constants at 60/30 min and the untouched default path yields exactly 3 meals, all provably inside both ceilings; an excluded plan now returns a typed code plus derived copy ("Nothing fits your 15-minute hands-on limit - the quickest dinner here needs 16 minutes. Raise the hands-on time limit in household settings to see more.") whose ceiling number tracks the household (10-min household is told 10) while the catalog number tracks the catalog; a short plan is separately worded ("Every excluded recipe exceeds your 18-minute...") and never says "nothing fits"; GET /plans/current no longer lies, while a household that never planned still correctly 404s. The hard filter was NOT weakened - the old 900s/1800s defaults still exclude all six recipes. RESIDUAL, recorded not hidden: no web file reads shortfall/is_empty/is_partial, because the plan screen (T-016) does not exist yet, so the honest explanation currently reaches no user. T-016 acceptance was amended at cycle 13 to require rendering it.

Prep contradicts the grocery list. handleGetPrep calls derivePrepPlan on the raw recipe without scaling to target_servings, so at household_size 2 the grocery list says 450 g chicken and 2 potatoes while the prep screen says 900 g and 4. Conductor-reproduced cycle 12 (cycle-012-verify-lookfindings.txt lines 22-30). Filed as T-043. Directly undermines the traceability the grocery must-have exists for. RESOLVED at cycle 17 by T-043, CONDUCTOR-VERIFIED by a gate that imports no domain code at all (D-26): it reads data/recipes/*.json off disk, re-derives every expected quantity with BigInt rational arithmetic written inside the gate, and compares against the live HTTP response — so a bug inside scale.ts could not pass both the builder tests and mine. Journal cycle 17, result line "T-043 -> done. TWENTY-ONE verified of 62 filed." NOTE ON THIS EDIT: the resolution was earned and evidenced at cycle 17; the known_issues entry was simply never updated to match. Carried forward at cycle 22 (recycle bookkeeping), not re-verified now.

A constrained household dead-ends. handleSwap requires exactly three active meals, so a 1- or 2-meal plan (which today is what a time-limited household gets) returns 409 plan_incomplete forever with no way to change anything. Filed as T-045. Compounds KI-7: the users most likely to hit the empty/partial plan are exactly those who cannot then swap out of it. RESOLVED at cycle 19 by T-045, CONDUCTOR-VERIFIED by a fresh 22-check gate authored after the builder returned (/opt/swarm/runs/cycle-019-gate.mjs rev3, output .swarm/runs/cycle-019-verify-T-045.txt, 22/22). The permanent 409 is gone: a 1-meal plan and a 2-meal plan each return 200 with 3 real ranked alternatives (H6b, H5b), a zero-meal plan still fails loudly with 409 plan_incomplete (H9), and an unoccupied slot returns 409 slot_not_active rather than a 500 or a silent swap (H8a/H8b). RESIDUAL, recorded not hidden: on the shipped SIX-recipe catalog a genuinely planner-produced short plan still has an EMPTY candidate pool, because the planner's short plan already contains every survivor - so the constrained household now gets an honest 200 with none_reason 'no_candidates_in_pool' and the copy 'There are no other eligible recipes to offer right now.' instead of a permanent 409. The mechanism is fixed and the dead end is gone; real CHOICE for that household waits on catalog size (T-010/T-011, recipes 7-30). This is a catalog limitation, not a swap defect, and it is not claimed as more than it is.

The grocery list is not shoppable: quantities render as raw rationals such as "Olive oil 44 12376473/25600000 ml" and "Honey 4 25176473/32000000 ml". Ten such values on a 22-line list. Root cause is one call site (grocery.js calls formatQuantity without maxFracDigits). Filed as T-052. This is the only thing standing between the grocery ledger and done - the other 11 gate checks, including full DoD-5 traceability, pass. RESOLVED at cycle 15 by T-052, CONDUCTOR-VERIFIED and specifically proven GENERAL rather than tuned to its own check (journal cycle 15, "T-052 -> DONE, and proven general rather than tuned to its own check"; result line "T-019 -> done. T-052 -> done. NINETEEN verified of 58 filed."). NOTE ON THIS EDIT: the resolution was earned and evidenced at cycle 15; the known_issues entry was never updated to match. Carried forward at cycle 22 (recycle bookkeeping), not re-verified now.

No client JavaScript has ever been typechecked. tsconfig include is [domain,server,tests]; tsc --listFiles reports zero files under web/js. Every "typecheck passes" claim about a web file this run was true but vacuous. Filed as T-054.
known_issues.resolution: Closed by T-054 at cycle 25. tsconfig.web.json typechecks all 10 web/js files under strict + checkJs, wired into npm test as typecheck:web. Proven failable: a real semantic error injected into ui.js, grocery.js and cook.js each broke npm test. Residual gaps filed as T-071 and T-072 — the client is typechecked, not yet fully typed.

known_issues.desc: Kitchen timers are unreachable in the running product. No code path anywhere in web/ or server business logic produces a timer_started event; only the validator that would accept one exists. Cause: encodeStepView never exposes a step timer duration, so the client has nothing honest to start a timer from. Rendering/ticking/expiry all verified correct at cycle 15 by injecting the event directly (C12-C14) — the way IN is what is missing. Filed as T-058. RESOLVED at cycle 24 by T-058, CONDUCTOR-VERIFIED by a fresh 15-check gate authored after the builder returned (.swarm/runs/cycle-024-gate-T-058.mjs rev2, output cycle-024-verify-T-058.txt, 15/15). encodeStepView now emits the recipe's authoritative timer_duration_seconds (verified against data/recipes/*.json re-read by the gate itself on all 16 walked steps), the client posts nothing but {kind:'timer_started', step_index}, and the server derives id, duration and absolute ends_at_utc. Proven end to end through the real HTTP API AND the real rendered screen — one tap on "Start 35 minutes timer" produces a live 35:00 clock with the accessible name "35 minutes remaining", the control withdraws itself, and a second HTTP GET confirms the timer exists server-side at step_index 2. The anti-derivation clause is separately proven: 3 shipped steps have timer != total-active, and the wire value tracks the authored one on those. Kill-safety re-checked here too (T9): the server process was closed and reopened on the same sqlite file, ends_at_utc identical, remaining decreased by real elapsed time. Failability proven rather than assumed: mutant M1 (field deleted) and M2 (derived as total-minus-active) were each killed by three independent checks, and routes.ts was sha256-restored identically.
